name: Doll short movie (wordless animated story)
what: A 26–35 s wordless 3D-animated story about one character moving through a few rooms of one home, driven by sound effects and a lo-fi music bed, where the other person exists only as phone text on screen and the product is used in close-up as part of the routine.

specialised.what: no song and no voice — the audio is a flat music loop plus a foley track of sharp one-hit effects, and the cut is built from the STORY's beats, not from an audio clock
specialised.why: the records measure music under 83% of the runtime as a flat loop (117.5 bpm, C major, laid-over, loud, 'none — steady' builds and drops) and only 5 non-verbal utterances in the transcript; there is no sung or spoken line for a clip to sit under, so the sung-story playbook's 'song first, cut follows the song' station has nothing to drive it

specialised.what: the music is picked from the bank (or made once) as a 115–120 bpm lo-fi loop at a fixed level, no sections, no bridge, no outro tag — the brand line is never heard, only shown
specialised.why: measured 'flat-loop · laid-over · loud', voice-over-music 0.3 dB, 'ends quietly'; the swipe has no sung brand line at all — the brand arrives as on-screen text (the brand name at 0:22 and 0:25), so the song playbook's bridge/outro-tag rule has no place to land

specialised.what: a FOLEY PASS is its own station after the clips: one bank hit per physical action, placed on the frame it happens (notification chime, popcorn scatter, fast ticking, pop, rubbing, brushing, fabric rustle, zip, fabric thud, wiping, wet slap, low rumble)
specialised.why: the sound sheet lists 13 cues across 26 s — roughly one every 2 s — and the mechanics say 'fast cuts and ASMR sounds keep pace high'; the effects ARE the dialogue in this shape, so they are planned like lines rather than sweetened at the end

specialised.what: non-verbal character vocals (laugh, hmm, gasp, oof) are made as 4 one-shot takes on the voice door, not a read — no script, no line parity
specialised.why: transcript T2–T5 are isolated reactions at 0:03.1, 0:11.0, 0:19.0, 0:20.0 and the voice card measures ~62 words/min 'consisting entirely of isolated reactions'; a stitched read would invent speech the swipe does not have

specialised.what: the second person is a TEXT MESSAGE on a phone screen — never cast, never rendered, never voiced; two screen scenes only
specialised.why: the roll sheet has exactly two S rows ('BOYFRIEND / I'll arrive in 1 hour.' at 0:02 and 'Sorry, I won't be able to come.' at 0:18) and the doctrine read says the other person is 'seen only as text messages'; this saves a whole second character's element sheet

specialised.what: a VANITY MIRROR set is the workhorse: one plain grey mirror-reflection background carries the whole product sequence (0:05–0:14), 6+ clips off 1–2 pictures
specialised.why: the frame map shows K04–K11 as eight consecutive eye-level close-ups, static camera, same bright even neutral light, same grey background; one set-up re-shot eight times is the cheapest possible block and it is what the swipe actually does

specialised.what: the clock is a repeating MOTIF insert, generated ONCE and reused with a different speed/push-in each time it returns
specialised.why: the same prop returns at 0:04, 0:14 and 0:16 with the same on-screen text ('12 / QUARTZ') and the same 'fast ticking' cue; two B-silent rows plus one in-shot appearance is one picture, not three

specialised.what: clips run 0.7–2.4 s (median ~1.0 s), so the clip floor is the model's minimum and the edit trims in — not 3–4 s clips
specialised.why: 18 shots in 26.98 s with 17 cuts; the frame map's own durations are 0.333–2.4 s except the 5.75 s final hold; a 3 s clip would be longer than almost every shot in the piece

specialised.what: the last shot is the one long one — ~5.7 s on the mask, resolving, then the brand text
specialised.why: frame map K18 is 5.747 s against a 1.0 s median, and the mechanics call the end 'slower at the start and end to emphasize relaxation'; the pacing rule is fast-middle, slow-ends, not uniformly fast

specialised.what: every camera is locked off — 'set down still' — with motion only inside the frame; the only camera moves in the whole piece are two fast push-ins and one fast pan
specialised.why: the frame map records 'held: set down still' on all 18 shots and 'move: none' on 14 of them; this both matches the swipe and makes the clips cheap, because a static camera on an animated set hides 360p softness

specialised.what: the product is rendered in the film's 3D style from the real product photo and HELD in close-up as the demo — label legible, used on skin, four separate product moments (dropper, jar, tube, mask)
specialised.why: the prop list names four distinct product items with on-pack text, and product_role is demo, not insert; the sung-story playbook's 'product arrives late as an insert' does not hold here — the product IS the middle of the film

specialised.what: on-pack and on-screen type is composed as a LAYER over a clean plate, never generated into the picture
specialised.why: the swipe carries readable text in six shots (the product names at 0:05 and 0:08, '12 / QUARTZ' twice, the two text messages, the brand name twice); generated label text is the single most reliable source of slop and the nearest playbook already records 'product label misspelt' and 'garbled background signs' as real failures

specialised.what: pictures at medium quality, fast tier, 9:16 at 864x1536 — same as the nearest playbook — but ~10–14 pictures for the whole ad because of set reuse
specialised.why: four settings, one character, one costume change, a static camera, and an eight-shot block on one mirror set-up; the sung-story playbook's ~20 pictures assumes six settings and a 2:45 runtime against this 26 s

specialised.what: no hook versions cut from the body — the opener IS the hook and the alternates are 2 s re-times of the same popcorn-drop beat
specialised.why: the roll sheet marks 0:00 A as 'opener: true' and the mechanics name the text arriving as 'the inciting incident' that 'breaks if cut'; the whole piece is 26 s, so a 3 s hook lifted from the middle would spoil its own ending

specialised.what: wardrobe and hair are a continuity CHECKLIST, not a free choice per shot — three states, and every clip declares which it is in
specialised.why: the cast card times the changes precisely: messy high bun 0:00–0:13 then long straight hair 0:14–0:26; bare face, then berry lip + heavy blush 0:12–0:20, then bare again 0:21–0:26; the t-shirt look, the dressed look, then the t-shirt look again — a wrong state is the obvious tell in a getting-ready story

stage_order: story beats (the wordless story, shot by shot — no lyrics, no script)
elements (one character in three states, four sets, the product in style, the clock motif)
storyboard (from the beat sheet's own clock, 17 cuts)
foley pass (one bank hit per action) + non-verbal takes + music loop
type layer (product labels, text messages, clock face, brand)

audio.voice_model: the voice door, one-shot non-verbals only (4 takes: laugh, hmm, gasp, oof)
audio.note: audio does NOT drive the cut in this format — the story's beats do. The music loop, the foley hits and the non-verbal takes are all laid under a cut that already exists.

song.brand_line: never sung — the brand is shown as type on the last two shots
song.sound: no song. One flat lo-fi loop, 115–120 bpm, warm synth + bass + drum machine, medium energy, no builds, no drops, ending quietly — from the music bank where a row fits; made once if none does.
song.music_level: laid over the whole piece, loud (the swipe's measured mix: music does not duck, voice-over-music 0.3 dB)

pictures.made_at: 9:16 directly at 864x1536; the clip is 360p so a bigger picture is thrown away
pictures.style_lock: 3D stylised realism — rounded forms, soft matte skin, exaggerated expression, visible pores and freckles, warm interior light; locked from the swipe's style read, formula first
pictures.product: image-to-image from the real product photo, restyled into the film's 3D look; shape, colour and label exact, then the label composed as type at the edit
pictures.plates: every shot carrying words (product in hand, phone screen, clock face, brand end) is made as a TEXT-FREE plate
pictures.count_target: 10–14 pictures for the whole ad: 2 living room (sofa wide, sofa close), 1–2 vanity mirror (carries 6+ clips), 1 bedroom/closet, 1 entryway, 1 clock, 1 phone plate, 2–3 product closes, 1 end
pictures.blocks: picture per SET-UP, not per shot — the eight consecutive vanity close-ups come off one or two pictures

clips.upscale: local Real-ESRGAN realesr-animevideov3 x3 to 1080x1920, crf 15
clips.short_clip: the model's floor is longer than most shots here — generate at the floor and TRIM IN at the edit; never hold a frame
clips.prompt_order: action line + style lock FIRST, then motion; nothing else
clips.refused_every_try: use the neighbour clip with a 7% punch-in
clips.camera: locked off on every clip ('set down still') — motion inside the frame only; the two fast push-ins (clock zoom, 0:04) and one fast pan (0:03) are the only camera moves and are done at the edit, not generated
clips.long_tail: one clip at ~5–6 s for the final mask beat

cast.reuse: one banked 3D character in this style carries the whole ad and every ad after it; the sets (living room, vanity, closet, entryway) bank as one apartment reused across stories
cast.second_person: NEVER cast — the other person is text on a phone screen only
cast.continuity: three declared states, every clip tagged with one: (A) messy high bun · bare face · oversized grey tee + black shorts + white socks; (B) hair down straight · berry lip + heavy blush · adds olive trench, black boots, crossbody bag; (C) hair down · bare face · back to the tee and shorts
cast.voice: no speaking voice — one non-verbal set (laugh, hmm, gasp, oof) banked with the character and reused
cast.product: ANIMATED STYLE RULE: the product is rendered IN THE FILM'S STYLE, image-to-image from the real product photo (shape, colour and label kept exact), held and used by the banked character; only the end card may be the real packshot. Real archive footage and studio renders in the body are refused for an animated style.

hooks.shape: the opener IS the hook — the relaxed beat, the phone lighting up, the popcorn flying (0:00–0:03). Alternates are re-times of that same beat (speed, hold on the shock frame, which frame the chime lands on), not clips lifted from the middle

captions.look: no captions and no spoken lines to caption. Four type layers instead, each composed over a clean plate: the phone text bubbles in the platform's own message look (sender name above), the product name on-pack, the clock face, and the brand word on the last two shots. Optional silent-viewer headline at 16% from the top on the control.

apply: style lock (every element and frame in the 3D style row)
clip words check (no words generated into any picture)
type-as-layer check (every readable word on screen is a composed layer)
continuity check (hair / makeup / wardrobe state declared and correct per clip)
product true to the real photo (shape, colour, label) and in the film's style
foley coverage (every physical action in the beat sheet has a cue placed on its frame)
skip: lip-sync / line parity on clips (nobody talks)
protected words / spoken numbers (nothing is spoken)

edit.method: video-edit machine cut on the beat sheet's own clock — 17 cuts in ~27 s, fast through the middle, slow at both ends
edit.reuse: the clock motif and the sofa set-up return with a different speed or a 7% punch-in rather than a new generation
edit.camera_moves: the two fast push-ins and the one fast pan are done here from a static clip
edit.end_card: the brand word over the final mask beat; a real packshot push is allowed as an alternate ending
edit.garbled_background_text: blur at the edit (gblur sigma 22) or punch in past it
edit.loudness: -14 LUFS, true peak ≤ -1 dBTP; music laid over at the swipe's measured balance, foley hits above the bed
edit.trim: clips are generated at the model's floor and trimmed to their 0.7–2.4 s shot length here

copy.source: the beat sheet (the wordless story, shot by shot) — there are no lyrics and no script
copy.why: with nothing spoken, the copywriter has no lines to work from and will drift to the brand files unless the story beats are named as the source

failures.failure: a clip blocked: no approved start picture
failures.fix: every clip's start picture approved before the clip run

failures.failure: 2 clips carried words that are not words
failures.fix: type is a layer over a clean plate, never generated; the clip words check holds them

failures.failure: the packshot stayed outside the frame zone after one fix
failures.fix: packshot framed at 9:16 in the first prompt

failures.failure: mouths moved with no voice — the 'talking, no voice' check held a wordless render
failures.fix: eye review of mouths (mouths_reviewed); in this family that check is a review, not a stop

failures.failure: the edit tool crashed: amix with 0 inputs; KeyError 'clip' in thumbs
failures.fix: no-voice edits pass an empty voice list explicitly; thumbnails from the cut, not clip ids

watch_for: the character's face drifting between the eight consecutive vanity close-ups — same person, same light, eight generations in a row is where identity breaks
hair, makeup or wardrobe landing in the wrong one of the three states, which in a getting-ready story is immediately obvious
generated on-pack text and generated phone text coming back misspelt or garbled — the single most likely slop in a format with readable words in six shots
the clock face reading something other than 12:00 the second and third time it returns
hands: four separate product moments in close-up, which is exactly where animated hands produce extra fingers or a product that passes through the palm
the product changing shape, colour or label between the dropper, jar, tube and mask moments
clips generated at 3–4 s when the shots are ~1 s, producing a slow, floaty cut that loses the panic the hook depends on
the model adding camera movement to shots the swipe locks off, which reads as drift rather than energy
the foley landing a frame or two off its action — the chime, the popcorn scatter and the wet slap are the piece's punctuation and a late hit reads as broken
the music ducking or fading under the non-verbals, when the measured mix keeps it loud and flat the whole way
the final mask beat going static because it is the one long shot — it still has to move (pats, eyes closing, breath)
inventing a visible boyfriend, a second voice or a spoken line because the story implies a conversation
the apartment's four rooms not reading as one home — different wall colour, floor or light temperature between the living room, closet and entryway
the popcorn spill turning into a particle mess that reads as a render error rather than a gag
the brand word arriving only at the very end with no product name legible earlier, leaving an ad nobody can attribute

cost.why: 26 s, one character, one apartment: ~10–14 pictures at medium/fast 9:16 (~$__), ~20 clips at 360p mostly 1–2 s (~$__), music one bank row or one make, foley from the bank, 4 non-verbal takes, hooks re-timed from the opener at $0 — a fifth of a 2:45 song ad's runtime at the same per-second settings, with the vanity block collapsing eight shots onto one picture
cost.measured: $__ (34 pictures $__ at xhigh, 12 Omni 720p 3 s clips $__; ledger.json) against a $__ budget

quality_bar: it is the same person in all 18 shots — face, proportions and skin read identically across the eight-shot vanity block
hair, makeup and wardrobe are in the right state for every shot (bun/bare → down/made-up/dressed → down/bare/tee)
every readable word on screen is clean and correctly spelt: both phone messages, both product names, the clock face, the brand
the product matches the real photo exactly in shape, colour and label, and is in the film's 3D style — no real footage in the body
hands hold and use the product plausibly in every close-up — no extra fingers, no product melting into the palm
the four rooms read as one apartment: consistent wall colour, floor, blinds and light temperature
every shot moves — no still, no frozen frame, no held last frame, including the long final beat
no camera drift on a shot the format locks off; the only moves are the two push-ins and the one pan
the cut is fast in the middle (shots around a second) and settles at both ends — the panic is legible without a word
a sound lands on every physical action, on its frame: the chime, the popcorn, the ticking, the pops, the rustle, the thud, the wipe, the slap
no voice, no spoken line, no lip movement that implies speech anywhere in the piece
the music is one flat warm loop at a steady level across the whole ad — no build, no drop, no duck
no second person is ever seen or heard; the other party exists only as text
no readable garbage text and no real third-party brand anywhere in frame
rulings: the owner (autopilot rulings, 2026-10-07/10): "The variations are the look, not the hook." — one locked brief, made in korean-doll / thai-puppet / plush-mascot
the owner: "A wordless opening is fine."
the owner 2026-10-09: the reveal is instant
the owner 2026-10-10: "you shouldn't be using real b-roll for this" — animated formats render the product in the film's style from the real photo; only the end card is real
the owner 2026-10-10: the doll short movie is its own family
